q: 1. The loss of head due to sudden enlargement is
explain: This loss represents energy dissipated through turbulence as flow transitions to a larger pipe.

q: 2. The loss of head due to sudden contraction, assuming coefficient of contraction as 0.62, is
explain: Based on (1/Cc - 1)² * (v₂²/2g). With Cc = 0.62, the factor is approx 0.375.

q: 3. According to Darcy's formula, the loss of head due to friction in the pipe is ............
explain: The standard Darcy-Weisbach equation is often expressed as $h_f =  rac{4flv^2}{2gd}$ where $f$ is the friction factor.

q: 4. The hydraulic mean depth or the hydraulic radius is the ratio of ............
options: area of flow and wetted perimeter
wetted perimeter and diameter of pipe
velocity of flow and area of flow
explain: Hydraulic mean depth ($m$ or $R$) is defined as the cross-sectional area of flow ($A$) divided by the wetted perimeter ($P$).

q: 5. The hydraulic mean depth for a circular pipe of diameter (d) is ............
explain: For a full pipe: $A =  rac{\pi d^2}{4}$ and $P = \pi d$. Thus, $m = A/P = ( rac{\pi d^2}{4}) / \pi d = d/4$.

q: 6. The efficiency of power transmission through pipe is ............
explain: Efficiency is the ratio of available head at the outlet ($H - h_f$) to the total head supplied at the inlet ($H$).

q: 7. The power transmitted through a pipe is ............
explain: Power is given by $P = \gamma Q H_{net}$, where $H_{net}$ is the total head minus friction losses ($H - h_f$).

q: 8. The power transmitted through the pipe is maximum when the head lost due to friction is equal to ............
options: one-fourth of the total supply head
one-third of the total supply head
one-half of the total supply head
two-third of the total supply head
explain: By differentiating the power equation with respect to velocity, we find that maximum power occurs when $h_f = H/3$.

q: 9. The maximum efficiency of transmission through a pipe is ............
explain: At maximum power transmission ($h_f = H/3$), efficiency $\eta = (H - H/3) / H = 2/3$, which is 66.67%.

q: 10. A compound pipe of diameter d1, d2 and d3 having lengths l1, l2 and l3 is to be replaced by an equivalent pipe of uniform diameter d and of the same length (l) as that of the compound pipe. The size of the equivalent pipe is given by ............
explain: This is known as Dupuit’s equation: $ rac{l}{d^5} = \sum  rac{l_i}{d_i^5}$, derived from equating friction losses.

q: 11. The power transmitted through the nozzle is maximum when the head lost due to friction in the pipe is ............ of the total supply head.
explain: Similar to pipe transmission, the maximum power through a nozzle is achieved when head loss $h_f = H/3$.

q: 12. The diameter of the nozzle (d) for maximum transmission of power is given by ............
explain: For maximum power, the optimal nozzle diameter is $d = ( rac{D^5}{8fl})^{1/4}$.

q: 13. The hammer blow in pipes occurs when ............
options: there is excessive leakage in the pipe
the pipe bursts under high pressure of fluid
the flow of fluid through the pipe is suddenly brought to rest by closing of the valve
the flow of fluid through the pipe is gradually brought to rest by closing of the valve
explain: Water hammer (hammer blow) is a pressure surge caused when a fluid in motion is forced to stop or change direction suddenly.

q: 14. A channel is said to be of most economical cross-section, if ............
options: it gives maximum discharge for a given cross-section
it involves lesser excavation for the designed amount of discharge
explain: The most economical section (or most efficient section) is designed to minimize the wetted perimeter for a given area, which maximizes discharge and minimizes excavation costs.

q: 15. The discharge through a channel of circular section will be maximum when the depth of water is ............ the diameter of the circular channel.
explain: While velocity is maximum at 0.81d, the maximum discharge in a circular channel occurs when the depth $y = 0.95d$ due to the large increase in area.

q: 16. The velocity through a channel of circular section will be maximum when the depth of water is ............ the diameter of the circular channel.
explain: Maximum velocity in a circular pipe occurs when the depth of flow is 0.81 times the diameter.

q: 17. The highest efficiency is obtained with a channel of ............ section.
explain: Among the common polygonal shapes, the trapezoidal section (specifically a half-hexagon) is the most efficient open channel section.

q: 18. If the depth of water in an open channel is greater than the critical depth, the flow is called ............
explain: When $y > y_c$, the velocity is low and the flow is described as tranquil, subcritical, or streaming flow.

q: 19. The critical depth meter is used to measure ............
options: velocity of flow in an open channel
depth of flow in an open channel
explain: A critical depth meter is a device used in open channels to measure the depth of flow by creating a critical flow condition.

q: 20. The flow in a pipe is neither laminar nor turbulent when Reynold number is ............
explain: This range is known as the 'transition zone' where the flow is unstable.

q: 21. The loss of head due to friction in a pipe of uniform diameter in which a viscous flow is taking place, is ............... where, Rn = Reynold number
explain: For laminar (viscous) flow in a pipe, the friction factor 'f' is given by 64/Re. Therefore, the head loss is directly related to this coefficient.

q: 22. Hydraulic grade line ...............
options: remains above the centre line of conduit
remains below the centre line of conduit
remains parallel to the centre line of conduit
may be above or below the centre line of conduit
explain: While usually above the conduit, the HGL can fall below the pipe centerline if there is negative (vacuum) pressure in the system.

q: 23. The ratio of frictional factor and coefficient of friction used in general equation for a equation for a head loss in a pipe, is ...............
explain: Friction factor (f) is typically defined as 4 times the coefficient of friction (f'). f = 4f'.

q: 24. Manning's formula is used for ...............
options: head loss due to friction in open channels
head loss due to friction in pipes flowing full
explain: Manning's formula ($V =  rac{1}{n} R^{2/3} S^{1/2}$) is the most widely used empirical formula for uniform flow in open channels.

q: 25. For a long pipe, the head loss ...............
options: at the entrance and outlet both are ignored
explain: In 'long pipes' (usually where $L > 1000D$), minor losses like entrance and exit losses are negligible compared to the major loss caused by friction.

q: 26. For solving network problems of pipes, necessary condition is ...............
explain: Solving pipe networks (like Hardy Cross method) requires satisfying flow continuity at junctions, energy conservation in loops, and using head loss formulas like Darcy-Weisbach.

q: 27. Hydraulic gradient is equal ...............
options: difference in water surfaces / total length of the channel
head loss due to friction / total length of the channel
wetted perimeter / total length of the channel
area of the cross-section / total length of the channel
explain: The Hydraulic Gradient Line (HGL) represents the slope of the piezometric head, calculated as the head loss per unit length of the pipe or channel ($h_f/L$).

q: 28. Hydraulic radius is equal to ...............
options: area divided by square of wetted perimeter
explain: The hydraulic radius (R or m) is a measure of channel efficiency, defined as the ratio of the cross-sectional area (A) to the wetted perimeter (P): $R = A/P$.

q: 29. In pipe lines, a surge tank is provided ...............
options: to relieve the pressure due to water hammer
to overflow the pipe line during high pressure
explain: A surge tank acts as a buffer or pressure-neutralizing chamber to protect the pipeline against water hammer effects when the flow is suddenly stopped.

q: 30. Most economical section of a triangular channel, is ...............
options: right angled triangle with equal sides
explain: A triangular channel is most economical when each of its sloping sides makes an angle of 45° with the vertical (vertex angle 90°).

q: 31. The most efficient channel section, is ...............
options: half hexagon in the form of trapezoid
explain: While a semi-circle is theoretically best, among polygonal sections, a trapezoidal section in the form of a half-hexagon (sides equal to bottom width) is most efficient.

q: 32. Chezy's formula is used to determine ...............
options: head loss due to friction in pipe
velocity of flow in open channels
explain: Chezy’s formula ($V = C \sqrt{RS}$) is primarily used to calculate the mean velocity of flow in open channels.

q: 33. Back water curve is caused if ...............
options: friction head loss is more than bed slope
pressure is due to weir in the channel
there is an increase in width of channel
explain: An obstruction like a weir or dam in a channel causes the water level to rise above the normal depth upstream, creating a 'back water curve' (M1 profile).

q: 34. For a most economical rectangular channel, the width of the channel must be ...............
explain: For a rectangular channel to be most economical (minimum wetted perimeter), the width (b) must be twice the depth (d): $b = 2d$.

q: 35. For a most economical rectangular channel, the hydraulic mean depth, is equal to ...............
explain: In an economical rectangular section where $b = 2d$, the hydraulic radius $R = A/P = (2d \cdot d) / (2d + 2d) = 2d^2 / 4d = d/2$.

q: 36. For a most economical trapezoidal open channel, the half of the top width must be equal to ...............
explain: A trapezoidal section is most economical when the length of one of the sloping sides is equal to half of the top width.

q: 37. The best side slope for most economical trapezoidal section, is ...............
explain: The most efficient trapezoidal section is half of a regular hexagon, where the side slope angle with the horizontal is 60°.

q: 38. When the pipes are connected in series, the total rate of flow
options: is equal to the sum of the rate of flow in each pipe
is equal to reciprocal of the sum
is the same as flowing through each pipe
explain: In a series pipe system, the discharge (Q) remains constant throughout all pipe segments (Q1 = Q2 = Q3 = ...), based on the principle of continuity.

q: 39. Power transmitted through pipes will be maximum when
options: Head lost due to friction = 1/2 total head
Head lost due to friction = 1/4 total head
Head lost due to friction = Total head
Head lost due to friction = 1/3 total head
explain: The condition for maximum power transmission through a pipe is that the head loss due to friction (hf) is equal to one-third of the total head (H) supplied at the inlet (hf = H/3).

q: 40. The discharge through a trapezoidal channel is maximum when
options: half of top width = sloping side
top width = half of sloping side
explain: For the most economical trapezoidal section, one of the conditions is that the length of the sloping side must be equal to half of the top width.

q: 41. If the depth of flow in a channel is varying slowly, then the flow is known as
explain: G.V.F. stands for Gradually Varied Flow, where the depth changes over a long distance.

q: 42. If the depth of flow in a channel is varying rapidly, then the flow is known as
explain: R.V.F. stands for Rapidly Varied Flow, occurring when depth changes abruptly over a short distance, such as in a hydraulic jump.

q: 43. For sub-critical flow in a channel
explain: Sub-critical flow (tranquil flow) occurs when the Froude number (Fe) is less than 1.

q: 44. Chezy's formula is used for finding... in a channel.
explain: Chezy's formula (V = C√(RS)) is used to calculate the mean velocity of flow in an open channel.

q: 45. A rectangular channel will be most efficient if depth of flow is equal to
options: twice the width of the channel
explain: A rectangular channel is most efficient when the depth (y) is half of the width (b), or b = 2y.

q: 46. A trapezoidal channel will be most efficient if length of sloping side is equal to
explain: This is a key geometric property of a most economical trapezoidal section (similar to question 496).

q: 47. A trapezoidal channel will be most efficient if
options: three sides of trapezoidal are equal
three sides of trapezoidal are unequal
three sides of trapezoidal section are tangential to the semi-circle
explain: The most economical trapezoidal section is one where a semi-circle with radius equal to the depth of flow can be inscribed, touching the three sides.

q: 48. Critical depth is the depth of water at which
options: specific energy is one plus minimum specific energy
explain: As defined in question 497, critical depth corresponds to the state of minimum specific energy for a given discharge.

q: 49. The velocity of flow, corresponding to critical depth is known as
explain: Critical velocity (Vc) is the velocity of flow when the depth is at the critical depth (yc).

q: 50. Hydraulic jump will take place if depth of flow is
explain: A hydraulic jump occurs when a supercritical flow (depth < critical depth) transitions to a subcritical flow (depth > critical depth).
